one_line: Paired masters of Buddhist logic and epistemology, debating perception and inference across the scholastic networks of South Asia.

appearance.age_look: Dignaga appears as a calm man in his late 40s with a medium, slightly scholarly build; Dharmakirti appears as a focused man in his mid 30s with a lean, energetic build.
appearance.face: Dignaga has an oval face, warm brown complexion, soft thoughtful eyes with a gentle half-smile and a neatly trimmed short beard; Dharmakirti has a slightly sharper oval face, similar brown complexion, intense eyes with a furrowed brow and clean-shaven jaw, their default expressions showing Dignaga’s quiet contemplation beside Dharmakirti’s analytical focus.
appearance.hair: Both have dark brown-black hair in a simple tonsure style: shaved crown with a short ring of hair around the sides and back; Dignaga’s side hair is smooth and close-cropped, while Dharmakirti’s is slightly thicker and more tousled, and neither wears headgear.
appearance.costume: They both wear era-appropriate Buddhist scholar-monk robes styled like 6th–7th century North Indian monastic attire: an under-tunic of soft undyed cotton in light beige covering the torso and upper arms, wrapped by a main robe (uttarāsaṅga) of deep saffron that drapes over the left shoulder and across the body, with an additional outer cloak (saṃghāṭi) of muted maroon folded neatly over the left forearm and around the back; simple cloth belts secure the layers at the waist, and modest brown leather sandals cover their feet; Dignaga’s robe edges are plain, while Dharmakirti’s maroon cloak has a subtle, era-accurate repeating geometric border pattern in darker maroon along the hem to hint at his later scholastic refinement.
appearance.signature: A single long palm-leaf manuscript bound with a dark cord rests across Dignaga’s left forearm while Dharmakirti holds an identical manuscript in his left hand with a slim wooden stylus in his right, both manuscripts having visible but undecipherable incised lines to suggest dense philosophical commentary.

ref_desc: Dignaga and Dharmakirti are two South Asian Buddhist scholar-monks with brown complexions, tonsured dark hair, saffron and maroon layered robes, simple sandals, each holding a palm-leaf manuscript (Dharmakirti also a stylus) in a warm saffron-maroon palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two South Asian Buddhist scholar-monks, Dignaga and Dharmakirti, standing side by side: both have warm brown complexions and dark brown-black tonsured hair (shaved crown with a short ring of hair around the sides and back). Dignaga, appearing in his late 40s with a medium scholarly build, has an oval face, soft thoughtful eyes, a gentle half-smile, and a neatly trimmed short beard. Dharmakirti, in his mid 30s with a lean energetic build, has a slightly sharper oval face, intense focused eyes, a furrowed brow, and a clean-shaven jaw. They wear era-accurate 6th–7th century North Indian monastic clothing: a modest light beige cotton under-tunic fully covering torso and upper arms, wrapped by a deep saffron main robe draped over the left shoulder, and an outer muted maroon cloak folded over the left forearm and around the back, secured at the waist with simple cloth belts. Dignaga’s robe edges are plain; Dharmakirti’s maroon cloak hem has a subtle darker maroon geometric border pattern. Both wear simple brown leather sandals. As signature props, a long palm-leaf manuscript bound with a dark cord rests across Dignaga’s left forearm, while Dharmakirti holds a similar manuscript in his left hand and a slim wooden stylus in his right, suggesting active debate and commentary. Use a deep saffron and muted maroon palette with light beige and warm brown accents, and keep the overall look dignified, historically grounded, and consistently redrawable.
